title: Minmax
comment: Minmax — Gradient descent/ascent can be inefficient in finding saddle point (Nash equilibrium) for min-max games, because of spiraling behavior. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nash_equilibrium

title: Geodesics Fmm
comment: Geodesics Fmm — Classic reference: Ron Kimmel, James Sethian, Computing geodesic paths on manifolds, 1998. Extends the fast marching method to work on triangulated surfaces. http://www.pnas.org/content/95/15/8431

title: Phi Diverg
comment: Phi Diverg — Csiszar divergences compare the relative densities of two measures with 1. Does not require any reference measure. Handles arbitrary measures (discrete or continuous). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-divergence
alt_text: Phi Diverg. Csiszar divergences compare the relative densities of two measures with 1. Does not require any reference measure. Handles arbitrary measures (discrete or continuous).

title: Lp Balls
comment: Lp Balls — The l^p functional is convex and hence a norm for p =1. It is sparsity-inducing for p<=1. The l^1 norm is the heart of the lasso, also known as basis pursuit. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasso_(statistics

title: Som
comment: Som — Classic reference: Teuvo Kohonen, Self-Organized Formation of Topologically Correct Feature Maps, 1982. Self-organizing maps of Kohonen define a map between a 2D space to the data, by minimizing a quantization error and a regularity penalty. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-organizing_map

title: Ica
comment: Ica — Independent component analysis estimates a mixing matrix leveraging the non-Gaussianity and independence of the sources. Solves a matrix factorization problem. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_component_analysis
alt_text: Ica. Independent component analysis estimates a mixing matrix leveraging the non-Gaussianity and independence of the sources. Solves a matrix factorization problem.

title: Nash Eq

alt_text: Nash Eq. Classic reference: Nash, John, Equilibrium points in n-person games, 1950. Extend min-max saddle points to several players.

title: Ot 1D
comment: Ot 1D — There exists a single increasing map between two distributions, it is the optimal transport, and it is defined from the cumulative functions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histogram_equalization
alt_text: Ot 1D. There exists a single increasing map between two distributions, it is the optimal transport, and it is defined from the cumulative functions.

title: Kernel Svm
comment: Kernel Svm — Classic reference: Corinna Cortes, Vladimir Vapnik, Support-vector networks, 1995. Defines a kernelized version of the support vector machine of Vapnik, Chervonenkis. Very popular for classification. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Support_vector_machine

title: Bregman
comment: Bregman — Bregman divergences are convex distance-like functionals that are locally Euclidean. Most algorithms handling Euclidean distances generalize to Bregman divergences. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bregman_divergence

comment: Alpha Shape — Classic reference: Herbert Edelsbrunner, David Kirkpatrick, Raimund Seidel, On the shape of a set of points in the plane, 1983. Defines alpha-shapes, a multiscale family of simplicial complexes that generalizes convex hull and is useful for to… https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_shape
alt_text: Alpha Shape. Classic reference: Herbert Edelsbrunner, David Kirkpatrick, Raimund Seidel, On the shape of a set of points in the plane, 1983. title: Law Max
comment: Law Max — The max of n independent Gaussians concentrates around sqrt(2log(n)). The max central limit theorem allows one to quantify this. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher%E2%80%93Tippett%E2%80%93Gnedenko_theorem
alt_text: Law Max. The max of n independent Gaussians concentrates around sqrt(2log(n)). The max central limit theorem allows one to quantify this.

title: Lorenz
comment: Lorenz — Classic reference: Edward N. Lorenz, Deterministic nonperiodic flow, 1963. Lorenz attractor is the set of limit trajectories for a simplified mathematical model for atmospheric convection. It has a fractal geometry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenz_system
